question.text: A PMS portfolio has 100% long-duration bonds. The PM wants to reduce rate sensitivity without fully exiting. Which of the following would she MOST likely do?

answer.text: Sell a portion and buy floating-rate bonds or shorter-duration paper
Buy put options on a short-duration index

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Simplest duration-reduction: substitute some long-duration for short/floaters. More long-duration or currency hedges don't reduce duration. **The Trap:** Adding more long-duration INCREASES risk; currency swaps don't change rate duration. **Cross-Exam Context:** Core rebalancing technique in IV; XXI-B tests choice. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Alternatively, short bond futures overlay achieves the same without selling cash bonds — tax-efficient if the client has unrealised gains.
